📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the uproar over the alleged use of generative AI imagery in “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” has taken a familiar path. Early responses to the Netflix film penned by Quentin Tarantino and directed by David Fincher have pointed out egregious examples of generative video artifacts sticking out in key flashback moments in the film — including one shot from the trailer where it certainly looks like a video AI program rendered a wagon the wrong way around.

Recent findings suggest that the criticism is of the use of generative AI in principle as a fundamental betrayal of the creative process — but it’s also of Fincher, as a director who, historically, has been meticulous with the level of detail and intention in every single shot of his films. In the early responses to Fincher’s latest, there’s been a lot of surprise and disappointment about this particular filmmaker being caught up in an AI controversy. Related Stories Trump Renews Backing for Federal Film Tax Credit as Lawmakers Push for Year-End Passage ‘Disclosure Day’ Did Its Biggest Stunts Practically, So the VFX Team Worked Hard to Look Invisible — Watch.

At first blush, his approach seems at odds with using generative AI video, which relies on regurgitated (and, it bears repeating every time, stolen) data. But Fincher has defended his use of AI to the LA Times as a way to continue to innovate on an art form that is, after all, just over a hundred years old.

According to recent reports, that defense really shouldn’t be surprising, given Fincher’s history with AI specifically. Although he’s been critical of generative tools in the past, Fincher admitted to using them (never publicly disclosing which) in the 4K remaster of “Se7en,” which the director described as a process of needing to remake the negative in order to battle the ravages of time (and the thousands of tiny scratches that would show up in 4K). “If you could see a 30-year-old negative and what it looks like even when immaculately stored — it was an enormous amount of fixing, just digs and scratches and cinch,” he told EW at the time.

That kind of image restoration technology was around long, long before the Anthropic IPO failed to save the stock market, but its level of precision has increased enormously in the past year. There were also sequences in the stored “Se7en,” though, where generative tech filled in gaps from the original. For one example, Fincher talked about a moment where a camera pan overshot the mark and changedh a shot. The performance had been good enough to use a technically flawed take — and, combined wit an unused take, allowed software to generate the missing information and restore the intended image.

“It ends up being the most thrillingly stupid fix in the world because if you see it, we didn’t do our jobs. And you probably won’t see it. You probably won’t be aware that it’s happened. But you look at it, and you just think to yourself, ‘It’s so nice that we can fix that kind of stuff today,'” Fincher told Collider about that moment in “Se7en.”.

Recent findings suggest that by Fincher’s own lights, then, the problem with AI in “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” is that people are painfully aware of it. AI critics might make a distinction between video restoration tools that work on existing projects and those tools being used because they can more quickly and cheaply generate originals that would’ve otherwise needed to be crafted by human hands. Having something AI-generated isn’t necessarily better than nothing when it comes to art, and choosing to AI-generate a Western chase sequence inside of, say, 10 seconds isn’t a solution to all.

Sources indicate that still, Fincher knows what he’s doing. This past week, he emphasized to the LA Times that he’s not a Luddite when it comes to film: “We’re talking about a thing that’s a hundred years old, and everyone’s going, ‘Stop. Pencils down. No more iterating. It’s not necessary to have at your fingertips the ability to change the color of that person’s eyes.’ Well, it exists. Should we not use it?”.

In a recent development, the answer is an emphatic “No!” to some And they can certainly be mad, or disappointed, or disheartened about Fincher’s decision to use AI tools. The one thing they shouldn’t be is surprised.

Sources indicate that the adventurous hobbit of The Lord of the Rings, Frodo Baggins, has made a triumphant return to gaming in a brand-newly introduced game. The last time we ventured into Middle-Earth for a video game was with the cozy title Tales of the Shire. This cozy gem focused on the calmer, less exciting side of the world, and gave fans a chance to slow down and enjoy the beautiful setting of the franchise.

Now, it's time to embark on a new adventure. Frodo and his friends once again leave home to defend the land from an approaching shadow army. The quest takes the LOTR's beloved characters into the physical world, and right onto your living room table.

The Lord of the Rings: Fate of the Fellowship is a new board game from Asmodee, in collaboration with the popular Pandemic System. The original Pandemic game was created by Matt Leacock, and has players working together to cure and stop the spread of a deadly pandemic that's spreading around the world.

Since then, the game system has served as a basis for many collaborations and expansions. Now, it's time for the Lord of the Rings characters to make use of the mechanically rich board game system to create a unique and infinitely repayable experience for LOTR fans.

Fate of the Fellowship is a collaborative experience on an epic scale. Players work together to complete ever-shifting objectives and protect the world from the approaching darkness. Each game presents different quests and challenges, all revolving around Frodo journeying to Mount Doom to destroy the One Ring.

Evade the Nazgul and Sauron's Eye as you make your way through the challenges with 14 events and 24 objectives that change every time you play.

Industry observers note that the Pandemic x LOTR collaboration can be enjoyed by 1 - 5 players, with a separate rulebook for solo fans who want to dive into the board game on their own. Each player controls two characters from a potential 13, each possessing special abilities that make them useful to Frodo on his quest.

Recent findings suggest that in a time when everything seems to be going digital-only, this game is packed full of beautiful physical components. The full game includes over 150 Player, Shadow, objective, reference, and character cards. There are also nine Nazgul miniatures and 13 character figures featuring some characters that will be familiar to LOTR fans.

Industry observers note that you'll also find a collection of enemy troops, an Eye of Sauron token, and plenty of tokens and markers. All of these are, of course, in addition to the dice tower and game board, which features an intricate and detailed map of Middle-Earth.

The Lord of the Rings: Fate of the Fellowship board game is available for purchase right now through the Asmodee website for $79.99. The game is presently sitting at a full five-star rating on the site, from 89 reviews, making it an instant hit. Fans of The Lord of the Rings and board games will find something to love about this collaboration between the Pandemic System and LOTR.

It has been revealed that as a certified personal trainer, I work with a wide range of clients who have lots of different fitness goals. But for my clients in their 60s and beyond, there’s usually one objective that drives their training: improving balance and stability.

Industry observers note that I recently started working with a 60-year-old client who wanted to focus on just that. She noticed that she was a little more unsteady on her feet than she used to be, and had a few close calls with falling. After a thorough check-up with her doctor, we began our work together with the following routine.

Sources indicate that these exercises aren’t just for seniors. It’s never too early to start thinking about your balance, so give them a try during your next workout. They’re appropriate for any fitness level and you won’t need any equipment to do them (but adding a dumbbell or two will always make things more challenging).

Check in with your doctor before trying any latest workout, especially if you have balance concerns.

In a recent development, these exercises aren’t hard, but doing them correctly is important. Beginners should consider meeting with a personal trainer or physical therapist for feedback and guidance on form, and to get modifications if needed.

According to recent reports, you’ll just need some room and an elevated platform, like a stair step, for this workout. Hang onto a chair or another stable surface for additional support if you need it.

Start by doing each exercise for one set of 10 reps. As your balance improves, you can add an additional set and increase your reps to 12. You can also use small dumbbells for the step-up to balance to ramp up the difficulty.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

These exercises can be done on their own or as a warm-up for other activities.

According to recent reports, you may feel muscle fatigue when doing this workout, but you should never feel sharp pain. Stop the workout immediately and consult your physician if you feel sharp pain at any point.

Here’s how to do the exercises:.

The exercises in this workout force you to find equilibrium when your center of gravity is maintained over a smaller surface area – either one foot for the standing marches, step up to balance, and side step to balance, or a narrow placement of two feet for the heel-to-toe walks.

It has been revealed that during these exercises, your deep core muscles like the rectus abdominis and internal obliques engage to stabilize and support your entire body. Your glutes and hip stabilizing muscles also work to keep the hips in a level position. The stronger these muscles are, the more conditioned they’ll be to keep you upright and sturdy during everyday movement.

Additionally, exercises like the step-up to balance strengthen key muscle groups in your lower body, like the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes.

In a recent development, while it would take a lot for any fantasy show to rival Prime Video’s Lord of the Rings prequel The Rings of Power, one of the streaming service’s upcoming series could manage this if the show fulfills its ambitious plan. Ever since HBO’s fantasy epic Game of Thrones debuted in 2011, the hunt has been on for the next massive small-screen hit in the genre, with cable networks and streaming services alike sparing no expense in their attempts to outdo the show.

Recent findings suggest that HBO’s adaptation of George R.R. Martin’s A Song of Ice & Fire saga set records with its unprecedented season 1 budget, but what seemed like exorbitant production costs back then appear quaint now. Not only have the official Game of Thrones spinoffs House of the Dragon and A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms attempted to replicate the scale and scope of the original show’s success, but projects like Netflix’s The Witcher franchise, Prime Video’s The Wheel of Time, and the three-season Lord of the Rings prequel The Rings of Power have outspent the 2011 series.

According to recent reports, nowadays, every major player in the streaming wars has at least one expensive epic fantasy franchise that is designed to replicate the breakout global mainstream success of Game of Thrones. That noted, even within this context, there is one upcoming Prime Video show that could make The Rings of Power’s billion-dollar vision look meek. Carrie creator Mike Flanagan’s forthcoming adaptation of The Dark Tower is even more colossally ambitious than these earlier efforts.

Industry observers note that the Dark Tower is far from being The Haunting of Hill House writer/director Flanagan’s first attempt to bring King’s stories to life onscreen. Before Flanagan rewrote King’s debut novel Carrie in October 2026’s hit miniseries adaptation, his earlier movies The Life of Chuck, Doctor Sleep, and Gerald’s Game were all adapted from King stories and novels. However, this doesn’t make The Dark Tower’s ambitious adaptation any less daunting.

The seven books of The Dark Tower series run over 4,000 pages in total, telling the story of Roland Deschain’s quest to reach the titular monument before the villainous Man in Black beats him across the desert and destroys the entity that holds time and reality itself together. Set between our recognizable reality and the post-apocalyptic Western setting of Mid-World, the Dark Tower saga is arguably King’s most ambitious work ever, blending horror, fantasy, Western, sci-fi, and character drama in its complex story.

Although The Dark Tower’s story is incredibly long, complicated, and ambitious, the saga also benefits from King’s crowd-pleasing prose and deft character work. Thus, the lengthy saga never becomes too overwhelming for the casual reader, which explains how the series stayed on the bestseller list even as later books saw King undertake some truly daring meta-twists that could easily have alienated many fans.

This makes adapting the books a daunting task even for a seasoned filmmaker like Flanagan, as translating the appeal of King’s saga to the screen could prove expensive, time-consuming, and difficult. Luckily, both Netflix’s live-action One Piece and SyFy’s acclaimed space opera series The Expanse prove this isn’t impossible.

Both of these earlier small-screen critical hits refused to condense their source stories, despite the creators knowing that the respective shows probably aren't getting enough seasons to cover all their material. Whether it is the incredibly complicated in-universe history of relations between the Martian Congressional Republic on Mars and the United Nations of Earth and Luna in The Expanse or the ever-evolving saga of the Straw Hat Pirates in One Piece, neither show has enough screen time for absolutely everything.

According to recent reports, crucially, however, neither show uses this as an excuse to start cutting out great swathes of source material and dropping or merging entire major characters right from the start. Thus, Prime Video’s The Dark Tower show has a blueprint to follow when it comes to bringing a massive, unwieldy tome to the screen unscathed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that conor Sheeran is a Movies and TV features writer for Collider. He has a deep passion for cinema and watches everything from the biggest blockbusters to the smallest indies. While he specializes in movies and television, he has also written about politics, culture, and sports throughout his career. Based in Latest York City, Conor is also a massive fan of the New York Jets, Mets, and Knicks. He is still waiting for any of those teams to bring home a championship in his lifetime. A member of the National Writers Union and the International Federation of Journalists, Conor is a strong proponent of press freedom and collective action.

Heist films are one of cinema's most timeless genres. Whether set in modern times, the 1960s, or the deep past, a good movie about people willing to break the law in exciting ways remains one of the most reliable forms of filmmaking. As Michael B. Jordan prepares to introduce audiences to a upcoming and updated version of a Hollywood classic, the original film that served as its inspiration is now available to stream for free.

Sources indicate that premiering in 1968, The Thomas Crown Affair stars Steve McQueen and Faye Dunaway in one of the best heist movies ever made, and one that remains endlessly cool decades after release. The movie inspired another remake in 1999, starring Pierce Brosnan and Rene Russo, which swapped the original's bank robbery for a more elaborate art theft, something that Jordan's upcoming remake seems to be incorporating. With Jordan's upcoming adaptation starring himself alongside Adria Arjona set to release early in 2027, there's no better time to revisit the original classic. Fortunately for audiences, it is now available to stream for free on platforms including Tubi, Pluto TV, and Roku.

Recent findings suggest that the central plot of The Thomas Crown Affair centers on Thomas Crown (McQueen), a wealthy businessman who appears to have everything anyone could want: He's handsome, successful, and enjoys a luxury lifestyle that many can only dream of. Despite his success, Crown finds himself incredibly bored with his comfortable existence. This boredom manifests itself in a rather interesting way: he orchestrates an elaborate bank robbery, despite having no need for the money. Unlike traditional crime thrillers that tend to follow criminals who are down on their luck or desperate for money, The Thomas Crown Affair introduces a criminal who is motivated entirely by the thrill of getting away with something extraordinary.

Crown's confidence is soon challenged by an investigator, Vicki Anderson (Dunaway), who begins looking into the robbery to discover who could be behind the audacious crime. What follows is a cat-and-mouse game between Crown and Anderson, leading both to realize the romantic attraction that builds as each learns more about the other. It's a fascinating psychological battle between two intelligent adversaries, a duel that is only more exciting to watch thanks to the performances of McQueen and Dunaway. McQueen's effortlessly charismatic performance exudes cool, and it's easy to see how someone could be swayed by his charm, while Dunaway is the perfect foil. She knows what it would take to stop a man like Crown, but she also struggles to resist the temptation to be with him.

The enduring appeal of a story like The Thomas Crown Affair extends far beyond just McQueen and Dunaway's performances. Norman Jewison's direction gives the film a sleek, immersive style through its split-screen photography and editing, creating a distinctive look. The styling, costumes, on-set location shoots, and incredible score set the stage for an unforgettable experience. The Thomas Crown Affair helped establish a format for films like Ocean's Eleven and Entrapment that followed later, so it's easy to see how timeless this movie is and why a modern remake makes sense.

Michael B. Jordan's remake will take inspiration from the original and the 1999 version with Pierce Brosnan and Rene Russo, swapping a bank robbery for art thefts. This will mark Jordan's second time in the director's chair following Creed III; he will also produce and star alongside Adria Arjona, Kenneth Branagh, and Lily Gladstone. While many heist movies emphasize action, often using it as the anchor for the project, The Thomas Crown Affair demonstrates that compelling characters with psychological tension can be just as entertaining. The greatest strength of both films was the romantic and sexual tension between their leads, and, judging by the trailers, Jordan seems to be following in their footsteps.

Jordan's interpretation will certainly bring its own unique perspective to the source material, but the original film with McQueen and Dunaway remains a must-watch and the gold standard. For those eager to sink their teeth into a good heist movie and see the one that started it all, it's available to stream and, best of all, it's free on Tubi, Pluto TV, and Roku. Needless to say, McQueen's crime thriller is still essential viewing even nearly 60 years later.

VSCO rolls out its first native Mac photo editor with RAW support, batch editing, more

💡 Key Takeaways
  • VSCO today released Studio Pro Desktop, its first native photo editor for Mac, bringing many of the firm’s familiar editing tools to macOS, alongside latest features aimed at photographers working with large numbers of images.
  • Professional and amateur photographers just got a latest alternative for editing and managing their photos on Mac with the release of VSCO Studio Pro, a native macOS app that brings the firm’s popular editing tools to the desktop for the first time.
  • More than that, VSCO Studio Pro integrates with the organization’s broader ecosystem of photography tools, allowing owners to manage their workflow from importing and editing photos to delivering finished images to clients through VSCO Galleries, without having to manually export and upload them to another app.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VSCO today released Studio Pro Desktop, its first native photo editor for Mac, bringing many of the firm’s familiar editing tools to macOS, alongside latest features aimed at photographers working with large numbers of images. Here are the details.

Professional and amateur photographers just got a latest alternative for editing and managing their photos on Mac with the release of VSCO Studio Pro, a native macOS app that brings the firm’s popular editing tools to the desktop for the first time.

More than that, VSCO Studio Pro integrates with the organization’s broader ecosystem of photography tools, allowing owners to manage their workflow from importing and editing photos to delivering finished images to clients through VSCO Galleries, without having to manually export and upload them to another app.

It also supports keyboard shortcuts similar to those found in other popular photo editors, making it easier for photographers familiar with those apps to get started.

Here’s Eric Wittman, CEO of VSCO, on today’s launch:.

Recent findings suggest that “Photographers deserve tools built around how they actually work. […] 75% of VSCO Pro members have used our presets in the last six months. Now those looks live on the desktop, with one connected workflow from camera to client delivery and nothing getting in the way.

In a recent development, the first thing owners will notice, and then continue to notice when using VSCO Studio Pro, is how fast it is. From changing the grid size, to sorting images, to applying presets by rolling the cursor over each of the 200+ presets, pretty much everything about VSCO Studio Pro feels as real-time and instant as it can be when dealing with large numbers of images.

As for importing photos, VSCO Studio Pro supports Apple Photos, local folders, SD cards, and external drives, and offers RAW compatibility with more than 800 cameras from 20 brands. Users can also choose whether to work with files in their original location or copy them elsewhere.

Under the hood, VSCO Studio Pro Desktop combines Apple’s Core Image RAW processing with the firm’s own Reflex image processing engine, which handles presets and editing adjustments.

Batch editing in VSCO Studio Pro Desktop can handle anywhere from two to 500 images at once, which is great for promptly applying the same preset or film-inspired look (including Kodak Portra, Kodachrome, Fujifilm Velvia, and Kodak Tri-X), or making adjustments to an entire set of photos simultaneously, with changes appearing across all selected images in real time.

It has been revealed that and speaking of presets, VSCO Studio Pro packs an exclusive one called IOE1 Pro, developed with photographer Joe Greer. IOE1 Pro, as well as VSCO’s other presets, allow customers to adjust the strength, color, tone, and contrast, further helping them fine-tune each look to their liking.

VSCO Studio Pro’s editing tools include the usual suspects photographers might expect from photo editing software, including exposure, contrast, fade, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, skin tone, temperature, tint, hue, saturation, lightness, sharpening, clarity, vignetting, and grain adjustments for strength, size, and color.

VSCO is also working to expand its toolset to include bloom and halation effects, curves, masks, and a remove tool for people looking for more control over their edits and to make more precise, localized adjustments to their images.

Also in the works are newly introduced organizational features, including projects for managing groups of photos, as well as culling tools that will allow customers to rate images with stars and mark them as accepted or rejected, making it easier to sort through large photo collections.

Sources indicate that once customers are happy with their adjustments, they can export their photos individually or in batches, choosing the file name, format, resolution, and compression quality. VSCO Studio Pro also offers resizing presets for web, social media, and client delivery, as well as the option to save the finished images to a folder of their choice.

And speaking of client delivery, consumers can publish their edited photos directly to VSCO Galleries, allowing them to share full-resolution images without having to export them and upload them separately elsewhere.

According to recent reports, VSCO Studio Pro Desktop is available today as a free download for Apple Silicon Macs, with full feature access requiring a VSCO Pro membership, starting at $4.99 per month or $59.99 per year, or a VSCO One membership. You can see it in action below:.

To learn more about VSCO Studio Pro Desktop, follow this link.

#51278. Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1147 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI.
  • According to recent reports, GTA 6 is absurdly large.
  • Recent findings suggest that alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most important tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

Recent findings suggest that alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

Sources indicate that you can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

Let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

File size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

Industry observers note that game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

Recent findings suggest that according to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

First, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

According to recent reports, also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

If you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

More importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

Recent findings suggest that the DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

The Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

Recent findings suggest that if you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for newly introduced hardware, this might be your best bet.

According to recent reports, xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Starting today, the Gemini app’s “tasks” feature, previously known as Spark, is now available for free owners after requiring AI Pro in the past.

Google previously referred to this capability as a 24/7 personal agent before integrating directly into the main Gemini app experience in October. Above the prompt box on mobile (or below on the web), you’ll see “Chat” and “Task.” The first option is the existing chatbot, while the latter lets you “hand off even more tasks to Gemini.”.

With tasks, Google’s “goal is for Gemini to save you time and money.” Google shared use cases like:.

With today’s announcement, Google is emphasizing that “Gemini is your best choice as a personal assistant because [your emails, calendar, passwords, photos, files, and payment cards] already lives at Google securely, and you don’t have to send it elsewhere.”.

Behind the scenes, Gemini tasks work in your own “hardware-isolated virtual machine” that’s sandboxed and has protections against prompt injection, while leveraging Google Safe Browsing when browsing the web.

Other safety features include having you confirm purchases and asking “clarifying questions if an instruction is ambiguous.”.

Powered by the latest Hydrogen model, free Gemini tasks are available in the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India.

  • Xiaomi has taken on the task of making the most out of that normally-wasted space on the camera bump by turning it into a screen.
  • But the question is not whether the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max's Back Display is interesting, it's whether it's able to justify its own existence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I have many gripes with modern smartphones, but one of the things that really grinds my gears is the trend of Godzilla-sized camera bumps on the backs of phones, Apple's doing it, Samsung' seems to be planning on it, and a lot of Chinese brands look like they've been hit by a rogue hockey puck. I've been testing the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max, which also has a large, iPhone-looking camera bump, but this time things are different.

Xiaomi has taken on the task of making the most out of that normally-wasted space on the camera bump by turning it into a screen. This is not the first phone to feature a rear-mounted screen, or even the first Xiaomi flagship to do so, but in a world of phones that all seem to feel and look the same, it's quite exciting to see a phone company offer something that helps its phones stand out.

But the question is not whether the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max's Back Display is interesting, it's whether it's able to justify its own existence.

Looking at the 18 Pro Max, my mind immediately jumped to the cover displays on compact foldables. The way the display wraps around the two main cameras is reminiscent of the Galaxy Z Flip 8 and the Motorola Razr. It's a little smaller than those screens, measuring 2.9-inches compared to those 4+-inch screens, but all three share a common purpose.

In a recent development, this is a way to use your phone without actually using your phone, using the smaller screen to look at basic information like the time or notifications on a smaller and more power-efficient display. At the same time, and as Xiaomi is keen to emphasize, it's a way to customize the look and feel of your phone in a way that cases and other accessories just can't manage.

My initial thoughts upon looking at the back of the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max and playing around with the screen weren't totally positive. I couldn't stop comparing it to the cover screens on foldable phones, and the fact that those screens are front-and-center when you take out your device. Xiaomi's screen is on the back, which is not part of my phone I tend to pay very much attention to.

But the more I used it, and the more I figured out that it wasn't just a glorified clock and notification alert, the more I realized that my initial reaction was the wrong way of looking at things.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

The idea that this is potentially a very valuable feature clicked when I opened up the camera on the Back Display. This allows you to take selfies using the main cameras, in a similar fashion to foldable phones, using the rear-mounted screen as a viewfinder. This means you're taking selfies with the 200MP main camera, rather than the lower resolution hole-punch camera on the front.

According to recent reports, I'm not going to lie, though. This isn't a fully-fledged phone screen capable of running all the apps and services that you've got installed. It is significantly more limited than that, and the difference is like describing the difference between a smart home hub and a tablet.

The home hub may be useful for its own specific use case, but it doesn't have the same versatility or usefulness as a tablet running Android or iPadOS.

Industry observers note that the Back Display is great for glancing at notifications and the time, especially if you tend to leave your phone lying face down. It even supports Live Activities on a handful of apps, including letting you control music playback on Spotify. Plus, it's possible to customize your screen with different backgrounds and clockfaces, depending on what your own personal tastes and style might be.

So far so good, though I can't say that I've ever felt using my main screen for those tasks has ever been a particular burden — especially since I'm just not used to looking at the back of my phone.

Then again, if you already have a smartwatch, that's not going to mean much, since you already have the bulk of this information available on your wrist.

Xiaomi does seem to be hinging on Generative AI to turn this screen from a gimmick into something you'll want to use throughout the day, thanks to a built-in system that lets you vibe code your own apps.

In a recent development, anyone that remembers the flop that was Windows Phone will know that success of a mobile platform hinges on app support. Your apps give the system value, and without developers actively contributing to an app store, there's little reason for people to actually invest in one of your devices.

So how do you get app developers on board to add utility to a niche display on the back of a handful of phones? You don't. You hand that job to the customers, and let generative AI do all the hard work. So Xiaomi added a prompt-based system for creating Back Display apps from scratch, as well as an App Store of sorts that lets you see a curated selection of what other people have created.

Options I can see include workout schedules, mini games, educational tools, timers, and all kinds of different options, though I have no idea how effective or accurate they actually are compared to full-coded apps. Still, it's nice to see that there's a way to improve the usefulness of the Back Display — even if it would be nice to have proper Android apps on offer.

It has been revealed that I found that basic prompts did work, but the more detail you could offer the better the outcome. Xiaomi can "polish" your prompt to better your chances of generating a usable app.

However, this does not guarantee that the app would successfully generate — or that it would work. It took me multiple attempts to create a Doom clone, and even when it did, I kept getting killed off by a monster hiding out of my line of sight.

So it's not quite as painless as having a developer-made app, and playing games on a small screen isn't ideal. But in the absence of additional features, this system is fairly good at filling that niche.

Recent findings suggest that I've spent my entire life looking at the front of my phone, and never really concerning myself with what's on the back. Even in the pre-smartphone era the screen was everything, whereas the back was just... not vital. If rear screens start to take off, that could change the way people interact with their phones in a big way. And that's obviously going to take a lot of getting used to.

Sources indicate that that's probably the biggest hurdle these rear screens will face. There's certainly no shortage of utility, especially with the generative AI apps. It's just reprogramming user habits to glance at the back of the phone rather than looking at their main display. It's going to be an uphill battle to convince people that these screens are worth it, especially when they have to compete with wearables.

Industry observers note that if it weren't for the AI apps I'd say these screens don't have much of a chance. I'm not convinced that they will take off, aside from a few niche gimmicks, but at least they have some sort of unique selling point to work with.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday is usually a great time to grab a new e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a substantial discount are low. But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for around $55.

If you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is currently 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Recent findings suggest that xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink quickly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

The X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

Sources indicate that these upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 launched at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also notable to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing fresh firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. OpenAI kicked off the GPT-6 generation with Astra in September, then upgraded Sol to GPT-6.1 a few weeks later at DevDay.

Today, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol are coming to ChatGPT Work and Codex together. OpenAI says both can finish demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so you can get more done before hitting your usage limit.

Astra is still the model OpenAI recommends for your hardest projects.

Recent findings suggest that say you have a screenshot of a slide and want the rest of your presentation to look like it. OpenAI says GPT-6.2 Astra can use that screenshot as a template and match the layout, colors, and even the font size.

On the Codex side, OpenAI notes Astra is better at making and testing changes in an existing project.

“Early testers reported cleaner code style and more focused tests, with fewer rounds of revision,” OpenAI states.

Sol is the more affordable model for everyday coding and writing, and it gets surprisingly close to Astra on one coding test.

Cognition’s FrontierCode 2.0 measures whether changes to real codebases are good enough for maintainers to merge.

With both models at maximum reasoning effort, OpenAI says Sol came within half a point of Astra at about one-fifth the cost.

Some of you have been asking very politely. Some of you have just been asking.GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are now available.Super efficient and built to perform where it counts—the real world.https://t.co/qr2iP0GpfX pic.twitter.com/jLCyVIws2Y.

Both models are available starting today in ChatGPT Work and Codex on Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu.

In a recent development, the $200/month Pro plan also gets Ultrafast mode for the first time with Sol. The $500/month Pro plan gets Ultrafast on both models, as do eligible Enterprise and Edu workspaces once an admin enables it.

How fast is Ultrafast? OpenAI says it can generate tokens at up to 4.5 times the standard rate on either model, although it uses more of your allowance. You can switch speeds from the model picker.

Developers can use both models through the API today as well. Astra’s standard input and output prices are 20% lower than with GPT-6 Astra, while Sol keeps its GPT-6.1 pricing.

I slept on the Helix Cooling Memory Foam Pillow for a week and performed a series of objective and subjective tests, following our pillow testing methodology.

The Saatva Cloud Memory Foam Pillow arrived in a clear plastic bag within a cardboard box. It wasn’t vacuum sealed, meaning when I pulled it out of the plastic bag, it was ready to be slept on.

There weren’t any noticeable off-gassing smells when I pulled it from the packaging, but to be fair, I was really congested during the testing period because of hay fever.

However, when I slept on the pillow, there was an almond smell to it, which is a fairly common off-gassing scent for memory foam products.

The shredded fill of this pillow spreads when weight is placed on it, but not enough that my head sunk down to the bed.

As I moved my head on the pillow, the pillow felt malleable and soft, hugging my head in a comforting way. I particularly like how this pillow feels when I’m lying on my back and stomach, as my head sinks enough to align my spine, lulling me to sleep promptly.

I can sleep on my side with the standard loft size. However, I think the high loft would be better if I was strictly a side sleeper.

When the pillow eventually breaks down, I can see myself sleeping on my side less and less with this pillow and reverting to my back or stomach. Those with broad shoulders should choose the high loft size from the get-go.

I placed a 15lb weight in the center of the pillow, and it sunk over an inch. That makes sense considering the foams inside are shredded. When I lifted the dumbbell, the pillow sprung back into shape immediately, which is a good sign of the its durability.

Industry observers note that I didn’t wake up hot or sweaty when sleeping on the Saatva Cloud Memory Foam Pillow, and that’s all thanks to Saatva’s temperature regulation. Memory foam is a far more heat-retaining material than natural latex, so to mitigate any overheating challenges, Saatva utilized organic cotton for the cover — which is breathable — and shredded the memory foam and latex interior fill so air could weave its way through and keep my temperature neutral at night.

During the beginning of testing, I was sleeping without the air-conditioner and just a fan, so it was about 75 degrees in my house when I fell asleep at night and around 70 degrees when I woke up in the morning. The fact that heat did not build up during that time was very promising, and most likely what you can expect throughout the year.

A good rule of thumb: replace your pillows every two years and keep an eye on how rapidly your pillow bounces back over time.

This can be done by folding your pillow in half. A slow bounce back means the fill has worn down. Until the pillow breaks down, maintenance will ensure it lasts longer.

You can’t throw the memory foam and latex fill into the wash, but you can spot clean it if you need to.

✅ You like to try your pillow for a decent amount of time: Saatva lets buyers test a pillow for 45 days. If you don’t like it, Saatva will accept a return and give you a full refund.

❌ You prefer organic materials: This pillow does have some memory foam and while it’s CertiPUR-US certified, that doesn’t mean its free of toxins or VOCs, only that it’s low enough to be considered “safe.” Neither the natural latex, nor the organic cotton used in the fill and the cover are certified as organic despite claims by Saatva.

❌ You like to customize the size of your pillow: While you can order this pillow in high or low loft, unfortunately, Saatva didn’t design it so you could remove or add fill and thus adjust the height in your own home.

❌ You like a supportive, firm feel: Your head is going to sink into this soft and cloud-like pillow. For a more supportive and firm feel, try Saatva’s Down Alternative Pillow.

According to recent reports, the Helix Talalay Latex pillow is a good alternative for those who don’t like their head sinking too far into their pillow as it’s made from a single piece of foam. Expect a bouncier feel. Made with Talalay latex and perforated with holes, this pillow will help you stay cool all night long. It comes in two loft options and you can get this pillow for as little as $111, which is more affordable than the Saatva Cloud Memory Foam Pillow.

It has been revealed that as the name of this pillow indicates, the Coop Sleep Good Adjustable Latex Pillow is adjustable. It's made with a blend of natural Talalay latex and microfibers, and comes with an extra bag of fill so you can add more if necessary and create the loft and feel you prefer. Our reviewer reports that the pillow is breathable and prevents heat from trapping. A 100-night trial and a 5-year warranty is worth having, too.

If you want buttery soft comfort for a budget price, then I reccomend the viral Squishmallows SquishPillow, which is just $29.99 in a standard size. Presently our No 1 budget pick thanks to our glowing SquishPillow review (which praised its plush comfort and reliable support), the SquishPillow comes in a medium, firm or soft.

Alex Temblador is a freelance mattress reviewer and writer who has tested a range of traditional and smart mattresses for Tom's Guide. These include the Sleep Number i8 smart bed, the PlushBeds Botanical Bliss luxury organic mattress, and our favorite cooling bed the Bear Elite Hybrid. Alex also reviews bedding and other sleep products for Tom's Guide, including the Brooklinen All-Season Down Comforter and the BeautyRest Black Luxury Foam Pillow. Elsewhere, Alex's work has been published at Dwell, Real Homes, Architectural Digest, and Gardeningetc. When Alex isn’t reviewing sleep and home products, she’s building her career as the award-winning author of two novels, Secrets of the Casa Rosada and Half Outlaw, from her home base in Dallas, Texas.

#51262. Why iPhone Duo wasn’t for me (but might be for you)

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (853 w)

Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5mac ↗ Open Full Page

Why iPhone Duo wasn’t for me (but might be for you)

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (853 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it.
  • I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands.
  • Perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it. Here are the three main reasons why the Duo didn’t work out for me, but might for you.

I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands. You can use it one-handed, but for me it’s not nearly as comfortable as the iPhone 18 Pro. It’s too wide and too heavy to be used for long.

Perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions. But that would be a pretty significant shift for me, as there are so many situations when I don’t have both hands free.

Sources indicate that if you already use two hands with your iPhone regularly—perhaps because you have a Pro Max model—then the Duo’s one-handed experience likely won’t bother you. But the more I used the Duo, the more I found myself missing my iPhone 18 Pro.

The biggest value proposition of a foldable is that it’s a 2-in-1 product, letting you have a standard phone but also a tablet-sized display that fits in your pocket.

Industry observers note that I totally get the appeal, and fully expected to love that hybrid design. But after two weeks of trying, I still struggled to find times when I actually wanted to unfold the Duo. And to be clear, that’s a me problem, not an matter with the Duo itself.

Sources indicate that I tried a bunch of apps on the inner display, and struggled to find use cases that—for me—made it worthwhile to open the Duo. But based on the feedback I’ve seen from most Duo owners, I’m very much in the minority.

Sources indicate that I know lots of people love the Duo for video, but I don’t watch much video on my iPhone. I almost never watch YouTube, TikTok, or Instagram Reels. And for demonstrates and movies, I stick with my TV screen and an Apple TV 4K.

Sources indicate that multitasking support on iPhone Duo works really well. But when I found myself needing to multitask, I still reached for my iPad Pro with Magic Keyboard attached. A keyboard-free product can’t replace my main computer (nor would I expect it to), and the Duo screen was too small to comfortably work on it.

Last year I bought an iPhone Air and absolutely loved it. Initially, the Air’s less capable camera system didn’t bother me, it was “good enough.”.

After a few months though, I started missing the Pro camera system more. Then I learned that my wife was pregnant with twins, and I knew I wanted the best possible iPhone cameras to capture their early weeks and months. So I bought an iPhone 18 Pro in September.

It has been revealed that I’ve been very impressed by iPhone 18 Pro’s Main camera upgrades, and it’s great having a Telephoto lens again too. Since having the best camera system is so crucial for me right now, I knew iPhone Duo couldn’t be my only iPhone.

It has been revealed that I initially planned to dual-carry the two models, using iPhone 18 Pro solely as a camera. But over and over I found myself wishing it was my only iPhone.

Recent findings suggest that I returned mine as well. Beautiful device, but functionally not very good.

Is the iPhone Duo camera good enough for most people? Probably so. But for this year at least, with my twins aging rapidly, it’s not quite right for me. If I loved the Duo for other reasons, I would just use both models. But since I didn’t, I’m happy to stick with the iPhone 18 Pro.

In closing, I want to explicitly state that I don’t think the iPhone Duo is a bad product, and this isn’t a “bad review.”.

Industry observers note that the iPhone Duo just isn’t for me. I get the sense, though, that it’s lots of people’s favorite iPhone in years. Apple created its most unique new iPhone model since the original, and there’s plenty to love about it. I’m very curious to see how popular foldables become over time compared to slab models, because each clearly offers pros and cons. But for me, at least right now, the iPhone 18 Pro is my model of choice.

It has been revealed that what has your iPhone Duo experience been like so far? Love it? Undecided? Let us know in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AirPods got a variety of fresh features this fall in iOS 27, several of which are exclusive to AirPods Pro 3 (now only $179). Here’s everything new.

Custom EQ is a feature that some AirPods people thought Apple would never ship, but iOS 27 adds it.

According to recent reports, with Custom EQ, Apple now lets you set your own sound profile for AirPods. Per Apple:.

It has been revealed that airPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully represent music, TV shows and movies, and calls. If you prefer a different sound profile, you can customize how AirPods represent any audio played.

Industry observers note that you can change the EQ by going to your AirPods’ settings ⇾ Audio & Routing ⇾ Equalizer ⇾ Custom. From here, you can adjust the sound profile for low, mid, and high frequencies.

Custom EQ is available on AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Max 2, AirPods 5, and AirPods 4.

Apple GymKit has been available for years, but only for Apple Watch. It lets you pair and sync workout data with compatible cardio equipment, like treadmills, ellipticals, indoor bikes, and more.

In iOS 27, GymKit expands to support iPhone using AirPods Pro 3’s heart rate sensor. My colleague Zac gave it a try:.

According to recent reports, the setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment.

Once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance.

For more details on iOS 27’s GymKit feature for AirPods Pro 3, check out Zac’s full hands-on below.

Read more: iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym.

For most AirPods owners, the single biggest upgrade in iOS 27 is Siri AI.

Siri AI is available on compatible iPhone hardware in iOS 27, and Apple made sure to expand full support for the AI assistant to AirPods too.

AirPods are essentially becoming an AI wearable thanks to the new Siri. It will let consumers do a lot more than the current Siri. Here are some key features via Apple’s website:.

In a recent development, earlier this year when AirTag 2 released, Apple brought Precision Finding support to Apple Watch for the first time. Until now though, it’s been limited to AirTag 2.

But with iOS 27 and watchOS 27, Apple expands Precision Finding on the Watch to AirPods Pro 3.

AirPods Pro 3’s case includes the latest second-generation Ultra Wideband (UWB) chip, letting you find it with greater precision and step-by-step guidance right from your wrist.

With every batch of new AirPods features that debuts, the AirPods settings screen in the Settings app gets more cluttered.

But in iOS 27, Apple has a welcome fix: it’s redesigned and reorganized all AirPods settings.

It has been revealed that now, you’ll find AirPods settings organized into more categories and submenus, accompanied by colorful icons. It makes finding the right setting way easier and more intuitive than before.

Read more: iOS 27 revamps AirPods settings in a substantial way, here’s the latest design.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that amazon's Black Friday sale kicked off today, which means it's a good time to score some of the year's best prices on e-readers. Timing your purchase is now a bigger deal than ever (so to speak), as Amazon recently raised the price of basically every Kindle by $50 or more due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

Because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save substantial on a few worthy Kindle alternatives. Here are your e-reader best bets in the lead-up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

According to recent reports, the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. An upgraded version of the basic Kindle, the Paperwhite adds a larger screen, temperature-adjustable lighting, water resistance, and better battery life—and if you opt for the Signature Edition, you also get double the storage and no lock screen ads. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the organization introduced a new model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

If you want a great Kindle but you don't care about paying extra for more storage or getting rid of lock screen ads, the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is also a great buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors.

If you don't need the bells and whistles of the Paperwhite, you can also pick up the standard Kindle. It's still a very capable device, with good lighting, 16GB of onboard storage, and the ability to hook up your Bluetooth speakers to listen to Audible audiobooks. The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

It has been revealed that if you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

According to recent reports, if you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is presently $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

The newly introduced Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. Combined with the large 11-inch screen, this makes it a great device for reading comics or magazine articles as they were meant to be read, or marking up PDFs using the included Premium Pen. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

In a recent development, if you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. Discounted $30 to $229.99 at Best Buy, it's right now pricier than the Kindle Colorsoft, but you get a bit more for your money. While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

If you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, presently marked down to $200, its lowest price ever. It's got a 6.13-inch screen, so it's the same size and shape as your phone, and it has a crisp e-ink screen with a strong (if not temperature-adjustable) front light and 128GB of onboard storage. The best part is, it runs on an open Android system, so you can install multiple reading apps, including Kindle, Nook, Kobo, and Libby, and keep all of your books in one place. (Check out my review of the Viwoods AiPaper Reader for more—it's a nifty little device.).

If you don't have a large Kindle library, you're moderately tech-savvy, and you praise portability above all else, I can't recommend Xteink's line of e-readers more highly. The 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic is at its lowest price ever, coming in at just under $55, around $34 off the list price. Meanwhile, the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 is about a dollar more; that's a less-generous 19% discount. I own both, and while the Classic is definitely worth the current sale price, I actually prefer the form factor of the smaller X3 (at the moment $55.72), which is about the size of a library card.

If you're feeling tentative about trusting a seemingly no-name Chinese tech brand, read more about the devices in my review, or listen to the collected wisdom of the tens of thousands of people in the bustling r/xteink Reddit group.

It has been revealed that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Industry observers note that follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. #51256. Breaking: Epic accuses Apple of withholding 122,000 documents, seeks daily fines

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (944 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5mac ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Epic accuses Apple of withholding 122,000 documents, seeks daily fines

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (944 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that in a new filing, Epic Games accuses Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions and asks the court to impose daily fines until the organization complies.
  • As a result of the lawsuit Epic Games brought against Apple in 2020, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled in 2021 that Apple would have to, among other things, allow developers to direct owners to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.
  • Recent findings suggest that apple responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in a new filing, Epic Games accuses Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions and asks the court to impose daily fines until the organization complies. Here are the details.

As a result of the lawsuit Epic Games brought against Apple in 2020, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled in 2021 that Apple would have to, among other things, allow developers to direct owners to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.

Recent findings suggest that apple responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them. This, in turn, led the court to find Apple in civil contempt for violating its injunction. Since then, Apple has been trying to overturn that ruling, a dispute that has now reached the Supreme Court.

At the same time, district court proceedings will determine what, if any, commission Apple may charge on purchases made through external payment links. Apple submitted its proposal on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, and Epic is expected to respond after Apple completes its document production.

In a fresh filing, however, Epic is accusing Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to how it arrived at its proposed commission rates.

One of the many aspects of the ever-sprawling battle between Epic Games and Apple centers on document production.

In its latest filing, Epic notes Apple has repeatedly failed to produce documents detailing how it arrived at its proposed commission rates, accusing the organization of withholding materials it deems irrelevant to the proceedings.

Epic argues that Apple previously used questionable claims of attorney-client privilege to withhold documents during the contempt proceedings, but has now changed tactics.

Recent findings suggest that apple does introduce one tactical change from its prior campaign of delay. Whereas during the contempt proceeding Apple used bogus claims of privilege to evade its discovery obligations, this time Apple withholds thousands of documents on bogus claims of irrelevance. For example, Apple is withholding well over 99% of the documents returned by running the agreed-to search terms on the files of the four custodians Apple indicates decided on the proposed fee (Tim Cook, Eddy Cue, Carson Oliver, and Kevan Parekh (Apple’s new CFO)) and three other key individuals (Nate Barton, Alex Roman, and Phil Schiller). Apple claims these withheld documents are not relevant to this proceeding-even though they hit on case-specific terms such as “proffer,” “contempt,” “injunction,” and “link-out.” To put this into context, while Apple produced 632 custodial documents returned by these search terms (including families), Apple is withholding over 122,000 based on a claim of non-responsiveness. Moreover, Apple claims that it completed its production from the files of these custodians, yet its production does not include a single substantive email discussing the rates Apple ultimately proposed; any notes or communications reflecting what occurred at any meeting where these rates were discussed or decided; any internal analysis of the financial or business impact of the proposed commissions; any App Store profit and loss statements; or any support for Apple’s assertion that its incremental link-out costs are “essentially zero.”.

Epic goes on to state that “Apple cannot be trusted to fix this problem on its own,” proposing instead that the court order Apple to produce all non-privileged documents matching the search terms agreed upon by both parties, regardless of whether Apple considers them relevant.

Sources indicate that under this proposal, Apple would still be allowed to review documents for attorney-client privilege, but it would be up to Epic to determine which of the remaining documents are relevant to the case. Epic argues that existing confidentiality protections would prevent it from using any of the information for purposes unrelated to the litigation.

It has been revealed that given Apple’s position, Epic respectfully submits that the Court should order Apple to produce to Epic all non-privileged documents that hit on the Parties’ agreed-upon search terms, so that Epic itself can sift the wheat from the chaff. Doing so will avoid further delays and place no burden on Apple. Moreover, doing so would not raise any of the concerns that required Special Master involvement in the prior proceeding, namely concerns around the production of privileged Apple information to Epic. Under Epic’s proposed remedy, Apple would be allowed to continue its review for privilege. For these reasons, Epic asks this Court to order Apple to produce all non-privileged documents that hit on any of the Parties’ agreed-upon search terms by December 2, 2026 (one week after Apple’s deadline to substantially complete production), irrespective of any relevance or responsiveness assessment.

Finally, though Epic does not propose a specific dollar amount, it “asks that the Court impose on Apple a daily monetary sanction for each day Apple fails to comply after December 2, 2026.”.

Recent findings suggest that according to the court docket, a hearing on Epic’s motion was initially scheduled for November 24 before Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers. However, a new order filed today, which has yet to be made public, refers the discovery dispute to a magistrate judge and includes a notice terminating deadlines and hearings.

In a recent development, apple has three main Apple Watch "lines." There's the flagship, currently the Series 12, which represents Apple's mainstream wearable. For athletes and consumers who think they'll put their watches through some extreme scenarios, there's the Ultra line, currently the Apple Watch Ultra 4. And while both the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are excellent devices in their own right, they can be pretty pricey (particularly the Ultra). That's why the third category, the SE, is actually best for most people, and Lifehacker's choice for best smartwatch gift of the year. Better yet, the third-generation SE is currently $50 off ahead of Black Friday, perfect for most people asking for an Apple Watch this year.

The SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do. It, of course, has a heart rate sensor to keep tabs on your pulse, including high and low heart rate alerts; the ability to track dozens of different workouts and exercise types (including swimming, thanks to the device's water resistance); a sleep tracker with daily analyses available in the Health app; notification forwarding to check in on your alerts without opening your iPhone; and the ability to send and receive text messages.

According to recent reports, it comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch. No matter which model you get, the watch comes with the S10 chip, Apple's last-generation watch processor. While it isn't as fast as the current S11 chip, the S10 is more than capable of running watchOS 27. Apple says the SE 3 can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge, and up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode, with fast charging from 0% to 80% in 45 minutes.

The majority of the features missing from the SE 3 aren't essential. Apple's other watches have things like bigger, brighter displays, additional health tracking tools like hypertension alerts and an ECG sensor, longer battery life, and Audio Intelligence—the latter of which might be a benefit to miss, depending on who you are.

In a recent development, if your giftee wants or needs any of those additional features, Series 12 or Ultra 4 might be a better choice. But for anyone who wants the essential Apple Watch experience, the SE 3 is simply the best-value watch Apple sells right now—especially at this discount. Right now, the watch starts at $199 for the 40mm watch, or $229 for the 44mm. You can also save on the cellular versions of these watches: $249 for the cellular 40mm watch, and $279 for the cellular 44mm model.

According to recent reports, yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

According to recent reports, black Friday sales officially begin Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by Dec. 2, 2026.
